page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5.16xlarge is an instance type belonging to the general-purpose ecs.g5 instance family. It is equipped with 64 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs driven by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at a base clock frequency of 2.5 GHz. The virtualized hardware runs on a KVM hypervisor platform. The instance provides 256.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 4.0 GB RAM allocation per virtual CPU core.

The server includes a baseline network bandwidth capacity of 20 Gbps to support data traffic across cloud infrastructure. It does not include local ephemeral storage, relying on attached cloud storage solutions for persistent data needs. Additionally, hardware accelerators are not present, as the instance features zero GPUs. Dedicated vCPU allocation ensures consistent compute performance without resource sharing overhead.

With a balanced 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio, this instance offers high resource density for enterprise-scale workloads. The absence of local disk requires external volume attachments, which allows decoupled compute and storage scaling. The hardware balance fits general-purpose application servers, large enterprise web deployments, continuous integration pipelines, and intermediate database nodes that require substantial memory alongside high parallel compute capacity.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5.16xlarge is a general-purpose virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor within the ecs.g5 family. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz, it provides 64 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs and 256.0 GB of system memory, establishing a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The instance features a 20 Gbps baseline network bandwidth for sustained data transfers across infrastructure components. It includes zero local disk storage and zero discrete GPUs, relying entirely on remote network-attached storage for persistent operational data. The combination of high core counts and proportional memory capacity offers strong qualitative compute density without shared-resource contention. This hardware profile fits enterprise web applications, continuous integration pipelines, microservices clusters, and medium-to-large application servers requiring distributed compute and steady network performance.
